acceptance: NB-005 is emitted from sql/validation/name_binding.rs, alongside NB-003, via a check called from validate_query_scope immediately after check_duplicate_relation_names

Two SELECT items emitting the same output name are rejected at plan time for: explicit duplicate aliases; a qualifier-strip collision (SELECT a.x, b.x); and a #1918 generated name colliding with an explicit alias

The emitted name of each select item is computed by #1918's SHARED naming helper — not re-derived, not copied. If the helper cannot be reached from validation/ it is MOVED to a shared module, never duplicated, and plan/ is not imported into validation/
collect_output_names is neither reused nor modified — it returns explicit AS aliases only and is blind to the qualifier-strip case this issue exists for

SelectField::Wildcard is skipped, with a code comment stating case 4 is out of scope and why (needs schema; SELECT alias.* does not parse, #1931). Non-wildcard siblings in the same select list are still checked against each other

The message names BOTH colliding items with 1-based select-list positions and gives a remedy; the generated-name case carries its own distinct guidance
NB-005 is an error, never a warning
The doc-example corpus gate stays green; if it reddens that is reported, not fixed by editing example SQL
New tests extend the existing name_binding_validation_test.rs and name_binding_error_message_test.rs; any new file is registered in the parent mod.rs
./run-commit.sh --fast is green, and any cargo fmt rewrite it applies is committed

ORCHESTRATOR RULING (brief §4z) on the 2026-09-16T06:01:41Z STOP is applied EXACTLY, and to those three tests only. NB-001 resolution validation runs BEFORE NB-005 output-name validation, reporting whichever fires first. output_alias_later_does_not_exempt_earlier_bare_ref_nb001 is UNCHANGED and still passes — if it is red the ordering is wrong, fix the ordering not the test. output_alias_earlier_exempts_later_bare_ref has item 1 aliased AS amount_ref, preserving the exemption it pins while dropping an incidental output collision, and the original shape gains a new NB-005 test. duplicate_alias_spelling_does_not_strip_earlier_exemption keeps its query VERBATIM and converts its assertion to rejected with [NB-005] and explicitly NOT [NB-001] — strictly stronger than the old .expect(), which could pass for the wrong reason. If a FOURTH existing test reddens, STOP again; do not reason by analogy.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING 2 (brief §4y) on the 2026-09-16T07:56:41Z STOP is applied exactly, to those 13 and nothing else. NB-005 stays UNIVERSAL — narrowing it to CTAS/CSAS was considered and rejected. That is a deliberate divergence from Postgres/MySQL/DuckDB/Flink, which permit duplicate output names in a plain SELECT: in a streaming engine a SELECT's output is a materialised stream bound by name downstream, so a duplicate is unreferenceable with or without a CREATE wrapper. Class A (3) flip to asserting NB-005 rejection; user_column_named_like_a_generated_name_is_not_silently_merged is the COMPLETION of #1918's visible-not-merged contract, not a weakening of it, and duplicate_output_aliases_are_not_admitted_to_the_join_batch_path must note that its batch-path guard is now unreachable from SQL. Class B (8) get distinct aliases with every existing assertion unchanged, plus the two wrinkles in §4y (the SELECT * case must still pass; the PRIMARY KEY test gains a sibling for the colliding form). Class C (medium1_same_name_no_alias_collision_build_wins) is re-expressed via SELECT *, and if that does not reach the same merge path, STOP — NB-005 has then made a real behaviour untestable. Class D: editing docs/sql/functions/SELECT-ALIAS-REUSE.md:148 is authorised FOR THAT BLOCK ONLY, renaming the second alias to amount_with_markup so the alias-shadowing lesson survives; §3d's corpus scan claimed zero instances of this case and was wrong, which must be reported. A FOURTEENTH red test is a STOP, not an extension by analogy.
